title: Nine-Card Locate-the-Spectator Card Trick (Aldo Colombini-inspired) with 15th-Card Reveal
summary: This YouTube video presents a card-psychology routine attributed to Aldo Colombini, repackaged with a compact nine-card setup. The magician removes ace through ten to create a top-stock consisting of ten cards (with the ten of hearts singled out as a key card), then uses a free spectator card choice, bottom placement, predictable shuffles, and a clever pile-dealing sequence to force the spectator’s card to be the 15th card after a three-pile arrangement. The explanation emphasizes a largely self-working plot, a small setup, and a sequence of shuffles (including an in-jog shuffle, a Jay Oz cut, a Charlier shuffle, and an out-jog/reverse faro) that preserve order while enabling the final reveal. The host also promotes a live-stream Magic Masterclass on April 6 and airs promotional material interleaved with the instruction. The video contains explicit step-by-step procedures, timing cues, and a final reveal that the 15th card is the chosen card.
topics: shuffle and cut without disturbing stock

sections.title: Intro, promotion, and deck prep
concepts: call to action: like, subscribe, comment
sections.description: The video opens with promotional remarks, then introduces the trick and credits Aldo Colombini as the origin. It includes a promise of a live, paid masterclass on April 6 and invites audience engagement before transitioning to the card setup. The host frames the routine as a compact, highly teachable effect and begins describing the small setup required for the nine-card stack.

sections.title: Core setup: nine-card stack and the top stock
concepts: remove Ace through 10 and place on top
sections.description: The instructor explains a minimal setup: select any ten cards (A-10) with the ten-of-hearts identifying the top stock, keep the ten on top while the rest are ordered beneath. A simple shuffle is used to maintain the top stock position, followed by a suggestion of a casual false cut to reinforce the appearance of a random mix while preserving the critical top stack.

sections.title: Spectator selection, card placement, and initial handling
concepts: placing chosen card into a specific pack location
move of the chosen card and top-card positioning (10 of hearts) on top
sections.description: The spectator freely picks a card (example shown: Jack of Diamonds). The card is returned and positioned through a sequence of moves that keeps the 10 of hearts on top and ultimately places the chosen card near the bottom. An overhand shuffle is used to maintain the required order while letting spectators feel they have influenced the handling and shuffle process, reinforcing the fairness of the routine.

sections.title: Positioning the card ninth from the top and bluffing a random position
concepts: count to ninth from the top
place a card as if it’s theirs at ninth position
slide the remainder on top to hide the move
bluff about throwing the card into a specific position
sections.description: A key bluff is introduced: the chosen card is nudged to be ninth from the top, then the rest of the deck is manipulated to conceal the move. The deck is riffled halfway and the chosen card is supposedly inserted into a random position, providing justification for subsequent shuffles and cuts while not revealing the true placement.

sections.title: Final reveal setup: sorting into piles and 15-sum property
sections.description: The routine introduces further shuffles (Charlier, out-jog/faro variants) and a pile-dealing phase. The audience is guided to deal into 2, 3, or 4 piles and then pick up left-to-right. Remarkably, regardless of how the piles are formed, each pile sums to 15, a property the performer uses to justify the subsequent reveal and to reinforce the 'free choice yet predetermined outcome' nature of the trick.

sections.title: Wrap-up and call to action
concepts: final reminder and praise for the effect
sections.description: The host closes with a quick recap and a call to action to engage with the video and subscribe, followed by a teaser recommendation for the next related trick video.

featured_techniques.technique: Overhand shuffle that preserves top stock
Three piles summing to 15 as a structural reveal device
Final reveal: 15th card is the spectator’s card
Key card placement with 10 of hearts on top
